description: We’re a team of curious problem-solvers using NASA Earth science data to understand how our planet is changing. We bring together data analysis, technology, and design to turn complex trends into clear maps and visual stories that people can explore and understand.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

Aeolus answers one question for any place on Earth: is the climate really changing here, or is it just year-to-year noise? Pick a continent, country or province on an interactive 3D globe (or any 55 km grid cell in tile view), choose a variable, and Aeolus tests 46 years (1980–2025) of NASA MERRA-2 data. The answer is in plain language. For Diyarbakır, Türkiye, for example: "Getting warmer: +0.42 °C per decade, about 1.9 °C in total since 1980; the true rate is most likely 0.24 to 0.61 °C per decade, and the chance this is a fluke is less than 1 in 1,000."

Nine variables: air temperature, humidity, wind speed, precipitation, evaporation, surface runoff (experimental), soil moisture, snow amount and aerosols (haze).

HOW IT WORKS

- Each month is compared with its own 1991–2020 WMO normal and averaged into yearly anomalies. The Mann–Kendall test and Sen's slope give the trend, with a 95% confidence range.

- Every result gets one of three levels:

- No clear change: no direction or number is shown, so noise is never presented as a finding.

- Likely change: p < 0.05.

- Clear change: p < 0.01, and only when three separate checks agree.

- Change per decade or total change over the period, for the whole year or one season.

- By month: each month tested separately, with correction for multiple tests, plus "seasons then vs now".

- Climate fingerprint: all nine trends for a place together, "seen together" signals (e.g. warming with drying soil), and the most similar places in the country and worldwide.

- A change-point check shows whether change sped up after a certain year.

- World trend map, Time Travel (a year-by-year replay of anomalies on the globe), and rankings among countries or provinces.

- PDF reports, CSV downloads, shareable links, and a free public API (JSON, no key; e.g. /api/v1/trend?place=TR-21&var=T2M).

BENEFITS

Climate data usually sits in large files that need specialist tools. Aeolus gives students, journalists, local planners and curious citizens a tested, honest answer for their own region in seconds. It shows the uncertainty and the method, and every number comes with its source. It runs in the browser, works on phones, and is bilingual (English and Turkish).

WHAT WE HOPE TO ACHIEVE

We want people to move from "I feel it is getting hotter" to evidence they can check, share and cite: local climate change made visible to people who would never open a NetCDF file.

TOOLS AND DATA

Data: NASA MERRA-2 v5.12.4 monthly reanalysis (GMAO, NASA GES DISC; single-level, surface flux, land surface and aerosol collections), NASA Blue Marble imagery via GIBS, Natural Earth boundaries.

Software: TypeScript, React, Vite, MapLibre GL (3D globe), custom SVG charts, Motion; a Python pipeline that packages MERRA-2 into compact files; Vitest; hosted on Vercel.

“USE OF SUPER INTELLIGENCE”
